# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — created both capability files from an EMPTY seed; the headline fact is that a formula in a graded cell always scores 0

The seed was a true no-skill control: `prompt.md` was 0 bytes, so `_read_system_prompt` returned
`""` and **no system message was sent at all**, and `task_template.md` was absent, so the adapter's
built-in `_TASK_TEMPLATE` was used — which contains *"once that file exists, you are done"* and no
verification step. So this iteration is a creation, not an edit.

- **Changes I made**
  - `prompt.md` (created, 129 lines) — Rule 1 *answer cells hold literal values, never formulas*,
    with the mechanism (cluster A, 25/26 failures); Rule 1.2–1.3 *a pre-existing formula in an answer
    cell can't stand either; recover its value with a second `data_only=True` load* (cluster A-sub);
    Rule 2 *write the right Python type*, as a 4-row table off the scorer (cluster D); Rule 3
    *`answer_position` is CHECKED, not a box to fill* (cluster B); Rule 4 *sheet resolution:
    `sheetnames[0]`, not `wb.active`*; Rule 5 *don't write the output with pandas; openpyxl or
    `zipfile` XML*; working-style section — in-sheet header/example outranks loose prose (cluster E),
    integer-scaled percentage thresholds (cluster F), the `max_row` auto-vivification trap, never
    re-run a failing block unchanged.
  - `task_template.md` (created) — restructured the contract into **READ → SOLVE → CHECK** with the
    `{max_turns}` budget made usable (cluster C, all 26); **deleted** the "file exists ⇒ done" line
    and replaced it with "you are done when the Round-3 output is all-clear"; field-semantics section
    including the pandas-preview offset (`preview row i == Excel row i+2`) and the all-`Unnamed:`
    header-row warning (cluster E); the two-load `ws`/`wsv` idiom; and a copyable Round-3 check that
    **asserts no cell in the range holds a formula** and diffs the range against the input.
  - All 6 required placeholders + `{max_turns}` intact, 0 unknown placeholders, template renders,
    all 4 embedded python blocks compile. No task id, value, date or answer appears anywhere.

- **Expected effect + why it's safe, per change**
  - Rule 1 should move cluster A (25 tasks) — every one of them wrote a correct formula into the
    graded range and read back `None`. Safe because **0 of the 14 passing tasks write a formula as
    their graded answer**; 6698 writes a formula *plus* a hand-patched cached value, and the integer
    Rule 1 has it write is the same number it patched in, so graded content is unchanged.
  - Rule 2's type table should pick up cluster D (6 tasks) once A unblocks them. The "normalise only
    the comparison, write back the original value" clause is there so 463-17 and 416-15 don't change;
    the formatting sentence is deliberately soft so 560-12 / 6698 / 80-42 still do the explicit
    formatting work they pass with.
  - Rule 3 should move cluster B (5 tasks). Two carve-outs make it safe: *match an absence convention
    the neighbouring rows already use* (without it, **80-42 breaks deterministically** — it passes
    only because it writes literal `"None"`/`"N/A"` across ~7000 cells), and *clearing is right when
    the instruction's uniformly-applied rule covers the cell* (**382-10** must clear `A18`'s stale
    `=IFERROR(#REF!/#REF!,0)` to `None`, and the instruction never names A18).
  - Rule 5 bans only the pandas writers and explicitly permits `zipfile`/XML surgery, because
    **463-17 and 6698 both pass that way** (463-17 after its openpyxl attempt timed out).
  - The Round-3 check is the structural fix for cluster C: verification is now the *definition* of
    done rather than advice, and the `assert` makes cluster A mechanically impossible to miss. Its
    enumeration is clipped to `chk.max_row` because 80-42's range is `A2:L8000` = 95,988 cells and
    the unclipped version risked the 60-second block limit on a **passing** task (clipped: 12,012).
  - Turn budget is not a risk: the largest number of rounds any trace used was 6 of 30.

- **Building on prior RESULTS** — none exist. This is iteration 1: `LEDGER.md` and `RUNMAP.md` are
  empty, `prior_iterations/` has no entries, and there is no `rejected.jsonl` to avoid. I did read
  the repo's prior *experiment* champion for this benchmark
  (`docs/experiments/2026-09-26-...-gemma-4-31b/champion/task_template.md`) as reference; it
  confirms the ordered READ/SOLVE/CHECK shape, but I did not copy it — it never states that the
  grader does **not recalculate** (the fact that decides 25 of my 26 failures), and three of its
  rules are the exact blunt phrasings my passing-trace audit flagged as regressions here.

- **Refuted hypotheses** — nothing is refuted by a RESULT yet. Two of my own hypotheses were refuted
  by evidence during this iteration and should not be re-tested: (1) the six *"Excel error text
  (e.g. #N/A)"* tasks are **not** a separate cluster and are **not** caused by `data_only=True`
  round-tripping or by agent-written `"#N/A"` literals — no trace used `data_only=True` and none
  wrote such a literal; they are cluster A seen through the recalculated diagnostic copy, where bare
  post-2007 functions (`AGGREGATE`, `UNIQUE`, `TEXTJOIN`, `FILTER`, `TEXTSPLIT`, `MAXIFS`) resolve to
  `#NAME?` because the xlsx grammar requires the `_xlfn.` prefix. (2) There is **no environment
  fault**: the grader behaved consistently on all 40 tasks, and 463-17's 60-second timeout was the
  agent's own `ws[f"A{row}"]` auto-vivification loop, not infrastructure.

- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked** — all six got an edit, so nothing is knowingly left on
  the table; what's untested is whether the *reader* complies. The two tasks I expect to resist are
  43436 and 51-12: they need correct reasoning, not a missing fact, and I shipped only the general
  lesson behind each. 50768 (a 9-box matrix where 6 boxes must stay blank) is the single hardest
  cluster-B case and may need a layout-specific guard if Rule 3 alone doesn't take.

- **Plateau signal** — n/a at iteration 1. The lever used here is the biggest one available:
  content-from-nothing plus one piece of **code enforcement** (the `assert not formulas` in the
  CHECK block) rather than trusting prose, which is what the strong-tier reader guidance asks for.

- **Focus next iteration** — read this candidate's RESULT first. If Rule 1 lands, the remaining
  failures should be clusters B/D/E, and the next lever is tightening the Round-3 check (e.g. making
  the `changed`-set comparison an assert too, or adding a type-expectation line) rather than adding
  more prose. If Rule 1 does **not** land, the question is compliance, not knowledge: move the
  formula ban out of `prompt.md` and into the per-task template next to the write step, where this
  reader is far more likely to act on it. Either way, check the RESULT's `broke={...}` against the
  four at-risk passing tasks named above (80-42, 382-10, 463-17, 6698) before changing their
  carve-outs.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.925 Δ=+0.575 · fixed={12864, 267-18, 2768, 37378, 37456, 39046, 43436, 45635, 46897, 48588, 48620, 48921, 50768, 51-12, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 7902, 8942, 9726} · broke={560-12} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
